transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-12 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Laura (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Maya (Finovate VP Eng), Carlos (Finovate ML), Priya (Infra), Tom (Procurement), Aisha (Security)

Summary:
High-level discovery focused on dedicated reserved capacity for Finovate's customer-facing LLM features. Primary concerns: isolation/data residency, burst strategy for peak trading hours, expected scaling and autoscaling behavior, encryption/KMS and SOC2 evidence. Agreed to send pricing deck, security docs, and schedule technical deep dive.

Topics:
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs (cost predictability, isolation)
- Reserved GPU sizing, burst pool strategy, and autoscaling policies
- Network/VPC connectivity, KMS/HSM, audit logs, RBAC
- Benchmarks and pilot scope (latency/throughput targets, model variants)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, i'm samir from redwood inference, i'm the ae on this account.
[00:12] Maya: hi thanks, maya here, vp engineering at finovate, appreciate it. we want to understand dedicated capacity - isolation, guaranteed throughput, and how bursting works during our morning spikes.
[00:28] Laura: awesome, yeah, i'll take us through the tech constraints, i'm laura chen, solutions engineer. quick question - are you primarily concerned about multi-tenancy isolation or regulatory data residency?
[00:41] Maya: both, really. our payments flows have PII and card data that's tokenized, but internal policy wants dedicated GPUs behind our VPC; also we need clear audit logs for compliance.
[00:55] Carlos: to add, our critical path is inference latency for fraud scoring - 50ms p95 target on our short-context model (max 512 tokens) and throughput of ~600 qps peak per region. during market open we see spikes to 1200 qps for 30-45 minutes.
[01:18] Laura: okay got it. dedicated can do reserved pools with predictable throughput. we offer burst capacity options - a reserved baseline plus a capped burst pool that can be shared across tenants in the region, or you can buy dedicated burst nodes for absolute isolation.
[01:36] Priya: what about autoscaling? our infra team wants predictable scale to avoid noisy neighbor impact when the burst pool is used. we need to know policies and cold-start behavior.
[01:48] Jordan: we support fast scale-up on dedicated; typical provisioning is warm-backed by preloaded images and KV cache priming. cold-starts are a couple of seconds for a new container but model weights are resident on the GPUs for reserved nodes.
[02:03] Priya: couple seconds? for us that might be too much for the first request in a spike.
[02:08] Laura: for low-latency SLAs we recommend a warm buffer - reserved baseline sized to meet your p95 during normal spikes and then a small burst reserve for extreme events. we can also pre-warm the model's kv cache so that token generation doesn't suffer the first-token penalty.
[02:25] Carlos: how does kv cache priming work with multiple model versions? we run A/B model rollouts frequently.
[02:31] Laura: we support per-model version pinning. when you rollout a variant, you can prime the cache via a batch of synthetic prefixes in the pilot; we also have rules to keep hot prefixes resident. priming can be automated via our rollout hooks. apologies if the term sounds fuzzy - it's the prefix/key-value cache for autoregressive decoders.
[02:53] Maya: security - does dedicated live in our VPC? we need to control subnets and peering, and we use a customer-managed KMS.
[03:04] Samir: yes, our Redwood Private control plane allows customer-managed networking but for Dedicated we can provide VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on region. KMS integration is supported - we can use your customer-managed KMS/HSM for key wrapping.
[03:18] Aisha: and logs? we need immutable audit logs and token-level access logs for last 180 days.
[03:25] Laura: we provide fine-grained audit logs and can ship them to your S3 or SIEM. retention windows are configurable; for enterprise packages we support longer retention and tamper-evident logs.
[03:37] Tom: from procurement standpoint, what does the contract look like? reserved monthly commit and overage rates for burst?
[03:45] Samir: typical model is reserved capacity commitments (monthly or annual) for baseline GPUs, with defined overage or on-demand burst pricing. we also offer a hybrid where you commit baseline and can burst into a shared pool at discounted rates. i'll send the pricing spreadsheet after the call.
[03:58] Priya: latency vs cost question - if we pin to an FP16 quantized model vs an int8 profile, what are the tradeoffs for p95 and accuracy?
[04:08] Jordan: quantization trades off a bit of quality for big cost and throughput wins. int8 can give 2-3x throughput improvements on certain architectures, but you should run your eval set. we can recommend quant profiles per model and run the evals as part of pilot.
[04:24] Carlos: that would be super helpful. our model has subtle quality-sensitive heuristics, so we want to track regressions. do you integrate evals and regression alerts?
[04:33] Laura: yes, Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets and evals. we can send regression alerts tied to baseline prompts. we'll include sample eval harness instructions.
[04:44] Maya: sizing - we'll be running across two regions (us-west, us-east). can we pin a dedicated pool per region?
[04:51] Samir: absolutely, you can reserve capacity per region and set routing policies to route by latency or cost or region. for DR you can set automatic failover to the other region or to a lower-cost model.
[05:04] Priya: what about network egress and VPC peering latencies - any observed impact on p95?
[05:11] Jordan: peering latencies are minimal; p95 is dominated by model decode time and kv cache misses. we recommend colocating the serving pool in the same AZ as your API gateways.
[05:23] Carlos: pilot scope - we want a 2-week pilot with 100 baseline GPUs reserved to hit 600 qps and then test spikes to 1200 qps for 30-45 minutes. is that reasonable?
[05:35] Laura: that sounds doable. we'll size based on your model (token length, batch size). sample starting point: for a Llama-like 7B with FP16 you might get ~20-30 qps per GPU depending on batch and latency target, so 100 GPUs could be more than enough, but we need your perf trace to size exactly.
[05:54] Maya: okay we'll share traces.
[05:58] Carlos: do you support custom kernel builds or only your managed runtime? we have low-level optimizations in-house.
[06:05] Jordan: dedicated lets you bring your container with precompiled kernels in the private deployment option; in hosted/dedicated we run our optimized runtime but we also support custom runtime in Private deployments. for Dedicated hosted by Redwood you can supply a certified image for certain enterprise plans.
[06:24] Priya: what about isolation on shared hardware - if we go reserved but not fully single-tenant, what guarantees exist?
[06:31] Laura: reserved capacity means GPU pools are carved out for you; but if you want absolute single-tenant hardware we offer bare-metal reserved nodes or Private (on-prem / VPC-managed). there is a price delta.
[06:44] Aisha: regulatory - do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001? and is there pen test evidence we can review?
[06:52] Samir: yes SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 are available; i'll share the attestations and redacted pen test summary. for deeper audits we can do MSA + security addendum and support third-party assessments.
[07:07] Tom: procurement note - we may want a 12 month commit with a 30% up-front discount if we commit to 12 months and provision across both regions.
[07:18] Samir: noted. we can propose tiered discounts for annual commits and reserved GPU lumps. i'll include that in the pricing deck.
[07:26] Maya: how do you handle model rollbacks in a canary or A/B? downtime?
[07:32] Laura: we do canary rollouts with traffic splitting and automatic rollback based on latency or quality SLO triggers. KV cache priming is handled per-variant so rolling back doesn't require a full cold start if configured.
[07:46] Carlos: data retention - logs and input retention, we need to ensure PII is redacted and we have the ability to opt-out of retaining user inputs.
[07:57] Laura: enterprise configs allow you to disable retention or set ultrashort retention windows, and we support automatic redaction hooks before logs are persisted. we'll share the security doc that outlines retention controls.
[08:12] Priya: are there constraints on model size with Dedicated? any limit on >70B models?
[08:19] Jordan: you can serve very large models; we provide both sharded and tensor-parallel variants. for >70B you typically need multi-GPU shards and there's more planning around KV cache distribution; we'll include best-practices.
[08:33] Maya: latency SLOs - can you commit to p95 under 100ms for our short-context model during normal operation?
[08:42] Samir: we can define per-customer SLOs in the Dedicated contract; meeting p95 depends on model architecture and sizing. the pilot is the right way to validate and we'll instrument token-level traces.
[08:56] Carlos: instrumenting - what telemetry do you expose?
[09:00] Laura: token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, tracing, and error analysis. you can hook our tracing into your observability stack.
[09:10] Tom: quick procurement question - do you require an MSSP or is standard MSA enough?
[09:15] Samir: standard MSA with security addendum is typical, MSSP only for very customized deployments.
[09:22] Maya: any experience with banks or PSPs?
[09:26] Samir: yes, we have a few fintech customers; i can share anonymized references.
[09:32] Aisha: about encryption, you mentioned KMS, do you support envelope encryption with your runtime and HSM-backed keys?
[09:40] Laura: yes, envelope encryption supported, HSM-backed KMS can be integrated and we do key rotation support.
[09:47] Carlos: what about model caching between requests from different users - is there a risk of leakage?
[09:54] Laura: we partition KV caches per tenant and we have tokenization/escape hatches to prevent cross-tenant cache contamination. for extra safety you can configure per-request salt keys.
[10:08] Priya: operations - what's the ops runbook during incidents? do we get a dedicated CSM for enterprise?
[10:15] Samir: enterprise packages include a technical CSM and 24/7 support. runbooks include automated failover, error budgets, and paging keys.
[10:24] Jordan: we also provide playbooks for canary rollback, degraded-mode routing to smaller models, and graceful degradation to cached responses.
[10:36] Maya: can you walk briefly through a sample architecture forDedicated in our VPC?
[10:41] Laura: sure - (short pause) picture: customer VPC with private subnets, peering to Redwood serving subnets, TLS+mTLS, ingress through your API gateway, dedicated GPU pool in a private subnet, KMS calls to your KMS endpoint, logs forwarded to your S3. I'll share a diagram in the follow-up.
[11:02] Carlos: regarding throughput, you mentioned batching - is that automatic or do we have to change client code?
[11:09] Jordan: batching is automatic in the runtime with adaptive batching windows; you can also define per-route batch settings. your client code doesn't need major changes, just the usual concurrency settings.
[11:21] Maya: for the pilot, what data do you need from us to size properly?
[11:25] Laura: perf traces (token distribution and request timestamps), model checkpoints, typical prompt lengths, and expected concurrency profile. also your security requirements for KMS and VPC.
[11:36] Maya: we'll assemble that.
[11:38] Tom: timeline - procurement needs legal terms by end of month, is that feasible?
[11:42] Samir: yes we can get a draft MSA + SOW within 2 weeks pending scope.
[11:47] Aisha: any regulatory constraints for EU data residency? we may have EU customers.
[11:52] Samir: we can provision Dedicated pools in EU regions and support data residency controls.
[11:57] Carlos: about rollback again - in an A/B, how quickly can you switch traffic away if quality drops?
[12:03] Laura: traffic split rules are immediate and rollback triggers can be set to watch for latency/quality thresholds; switching is near-instant for the routing layer, but priming effects are something to watch for.
[12:14] Jordan: note - priming can be done in advance during rollout window to minimize degradation.
[12:19] Maya: okay, i think that's the bulk. any red flags?
[12:22] Priya: i want to see the exact warm buffer and provisioning times for autoscale. also an ops runbook.
[12:28] Laura: we'll include warm buffer recommendations and a sample autoscale policy in the tech notes.
[12:33] Carlos: we'll also need the eval harness to run quantization tests.
[12:36] Laura: yes, will send along.
[12:39] Tom: procurement question - do you support net-60?
[12:43] Samir: payment terms negotiable at enterprise. we'll capture that as part of the commercial thread.
[12:48] Maya: can you also provide an example SLA with uptime and latency credits?
[12:53] Samir: yes included in the draft SLA.
[12:57] Jordan: quick note on cost optimization - we can suggest batching and quant profiles to get unit economics aligned.
[13:03] Carlos: great.
[13:05] Maya: any closing notes?
[13:08] Samir: next steps recap: i'll send pricing + draft MSA, laura will send security and technical notes and we'll schedule the deep-dive for priming/kv cache/auto-scale. we'll aim for pilot kickoff in the next 3 weeks pending traces.
[13:23] Tom: thanks folks.
[13:25] Aisha: thanks.
[13:27] (meeting ends)
